samples.summary: DOCX importer banding is scope the task record explicitly deferred to a separate change
samples.evidence: The originating task (`docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md`, issue #1050) closes Round 10 with "Follow-up, not built here: the DOCX importer is an unaudited *producer* of the same bands. `docx-style-map.ts:50` writes `fontSize` straight from `<w:sz w:val>` … Auditing and bounding an importer is its own change." and Round 11 repeats "Unchanged from round 10 and still deferred: … the DOCX importer as an unbounded *producer* of `fontSize` / `lineHeight`". This diff nevertheless bands both fields in `mapRunProperties` / `mapParagraphProperties` and adds importer tests, and the task doc is not updated to record the reversal. The behaviour change (a malformed `w:sz` now drops instead of writing NaN; `w:line` clamps) also is not reflected in the canonical importer doc `docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md` (lines 282, 297 still state the raw mappings). Cost is scope discipline and a stale record, not user-visible breakage.

samples.summary: The v1 `PUT` validation contract in rest-api.md is not updated for the new write-time numeric repairs (and now contains a claim the diff itself contradicts)
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlidesBody` now mutates stored *values* on write: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `bandSlideCellNumerics` / `normalizeSlideInlines` clamp or delete `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `listLevel`, cell `padding`, `rowHeights`, `colSpan`/`rowSpan`, and **slice `columnWidths` to `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS`**. `docs/design/rest-api.md` (the canonical contract doc) still says the repair guarantee is "exactly the list above" of *absent-field* fills and that "the values inside a repaired collection … are stored as given, so a deck can still render wrongly" (lines 423–428), and that repairs are only ones "semantically identical to the value that was missing" (lines 379–384) — truncating a caller's column list is not. Line 435–438 also still asserts `GET`→`PUT` losslessness because "the read side … drops exactly the values the validator rejects", which this change's own new comment in `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts` explicitly documents as false for `lineHeight`.

samples.summary: `sanitizeDocStyles` (new read-boundary contract for the named-style registry) is recorded in no design doc and in no task entry
samples.evidence: The change adds a sanitizer applied to `root.stylesJson` at both read boundaries (`docsTreeToDocument`, `YorkieDocStore.getStyles`) that bands numerics, drops non-object `inline`/`inlineDark`/`block` sub-objects, and permanently reduces a stored `inlineDark` to colour-only. The registry's canonical design doc is `docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md` (§ `root.stylesJson`, lines 285–293), which is untouched; the new numeric-band section in `docs/design/docs/docs.md` (lines 198–260) never mentions the registry, and the task todo has no entry for it. Since the registry is written straight back out, this silently rewrites stored documents — a data-model behaviour that repo discipline (CONTRIBUTING / docs/design) expects folded into the canonical subsystem doc.

samples.summary: The new table-structure bands (`MAX_TABLE_SPAN`, `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS`, `MAX_COLUMN_RATIO`) are undocumented in the tables design doc
samples.evidence: `normalizeTableSpan` and `parseColumnWidthsAttr` change what a stored table means at both CRDT read boundaries and on the v1 `PUT`: a span above 1000 is clamped, a non-finite one dropped, and columns past 256 are discarded entirely. Their stated sink (the `expandCellRangeForMerges` fixed-point loop) is selection, not pagination, so the new docs.md section — which is framed entirely around row height and the paginator — does not cover them. Grepping `docs/design/docs/docs-tables.md` for `MAX_TABLE`/`normalizeTableSpan`/band returns nothing, and the row-splitting doc §1.5 covers only the height bound.

samples.summary: New design-doc prose states a band rule the implementation deliberately rejects
samples.evidence: docs.md line 222–223 says every band "is set at the range the editor's own controls can produce, so nothing a gesture can make is altered." The module header of `packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts` states the opposite as a load-bearing decision: "Every band covers the range of every *producer* whose output we accept, not just the range this editor's own controls can reach", citing Word's 1638 pt and DrawingML's 4000 pt against the picker's `FONT_SIZE_MAX` of 400. A reader of the canonical doc would conclude `MAX_FONT_SIZE` is 400 and that an import above it is out of contract.

The two functions differ only in what they return (the block vs. the containing `cell.blocks`). A single walk returning `{ block, siblings }`, or a predicate-parameterised walker, would keep one traversal rule for nested tables instead of two that must stay in step.

samples.summary: The band wiring is duplicated into the frontend's copy of the Tree parser rather than the parsers being consolidated
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` re-implements `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts`'s attribute parsing, and this change adds the same seven band calls to both copies (the comments themselves say "Mirrors `treeNodeToBlock`'s boundary in the engine"). Sharing the band functions is the right reuse, but the duplicated parser is the thing that will drift next — a shared `parseInlineStyle`/`treeNodeToCell` in `@wafflebase/docs` was available. Pre-existing duplication, not introduced here.
